description: Andrew-direct 2026-08-24 ~19:2xZ at the base CTO terminal, VERBATIM: 'Finally, there should likely be one final pass worked out here that covers scripting/data ops. Something that concerns me about Cottonwood is that for mdpf, they have scripts "allegedly" located in opal-data-mdpf whereas all the others have scripts colocated in the relevant opal-data-assets bucket location. I want to make sure that there is a separate project registered the purpose of which is to identify the pipelines, data flows, code locations, data locations, etc for the advisor intelligence (advi) pipeline per partner, as well as for the model portfolios (mdpf) pipeline per partner. The purpose of this project will be to quantitatively assess and verify these various pipelines and once ground truth is established for each, propose a "remediation" for each the purpose of which is one canonical structure and flow so that all paths are in pattern and unified on that basis.' (record org/tier1_exec/1.0.0_SA_CTO/deliverables/ANDREW_DIRECT_20260824_PIPELINE_CENSUS_ADVI_MDPF_PER_PARTNER_ONE_CANONICAL_FLOW.md). DELIVERABLE SHAPE: (1) the CENSUS MATRIX -- pipeline {ADVI, MDPF} x partner {49 Financial, Inflection, Cottonwood} x {repo code home, S3 code home / deploy vehicle, bronze/silver/gold data homes, trigger/schedule, served keys + route, IAM principal} -- every cell MEASURED on the right layer (Rule 22a: DESIRED = the maps (safe_deploy_core.py PIPELINE_MAP, lambda-source-map, EC2_MANIFEST), APPLIED = live bucket/function reads, EXERCISED = comp-pipescript deployed MATCH/STALE/MISSING) with denominators, never the declaration alone (Rule 4: the source map pairs a lambda with its repo dir; it does not compare deployed bytes to built-from bytes); (2) VERIFICATION per pipeline -- deployed bytes vs built-from, applied vs desired, schedule presence (a production pipeline MUST have a schedule); (3) per pipeline a PROPOSED remediation toward ONE canonical structure and flow -- the ratified form (Rule 17b: {vendor}/{firm}/{medallion} under opal-data-assets; product gold under portal/gold/{product}/{scope}/ as parquet; platinum serving under opal-data-portal-v2/platinum/; the S3-code standard; one producer per served key) -- PROPOSALS ONLY: each remediation is its own decomp/TO on Andrew's word; NEVER#2 (no cross-firm references) and NEVER#3 (served output never moves without never-widen sign-off) bind every proposal; 'in pattern' is judged against the ratified form, not the majority of what exists. FIRST CELL, MEASURED (MSTR 66312, observed on today's deploys -- ONE cell, labelled as such): (MDPF x Cottonwood x code home): the script build_cottonwood_mdpf_slice.py's REPO HOME is data/assets/scripts/gold/ -- IN PATTERN, the same shared home as the other trees -- and its DEPLOY TARGET is s3://opal-data-mdpf/code/scripts/assets_gold/ (the MDPF bucket he sees), DECLARED at safe_deploy_core.py:216 ('assets_gold': ('data/assets/scripts/gold', 'code/scripts/assets_gold/')) with shared_repo_homes {assets_gold, silver} and a comment written to stop the exact misreading ('s3 code/scripts/assets_gold/ <- data/assets/scripts/gold (NOT data/mdpf/)'). So the suspicion is INVERTED: the divergence is the per-firm DEPLOY DESTINATION, not the source layout, and it is a DESIGN TO EVALUATE, not a DRIFT TO CLEAN -- the two take different remediations (Rule 22a classification: deliberately-held vs stale-by-neglect vs two-homes-diverged). PRIOR ART (rung 2, cited not rebuilt): comp-estate threads (advi-bd / advi-inf / advi-cot / smartx / canonical-schwab); comp-pipescript deployed (all-trees, firm-separated sweep -- the exercised layer); NFRA_DEPLOYCENSUS (deployed-vs-built-from census, D0); MDPF_CANPLAT / MDPF_CANRTE (the canonical spine + dispatch authority); MDPF_PROVCANON (one contract across four scopes + both producer trees); MDPF_CHANNEL_INDEPENDENCE; OPAL_ADVIPOINTERS (the five-phase ADVI framework + per-lane 08-12 reports); the 08-05 estate measurement in CLAUDE.md 17b (top-level gold/ json/ portal/ code/ in opal-data-assets outside the grammar). DIRECTIVE HOME: D0 Infrastructure (scripting / data ops) -- CTO recommendation; register edit at MSTR.
